full_judgment: 4. The trial Court allowed pre-emption and that order was affirmed by the appellate Court. In revision the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, however, dismissed the petitioner, case for pre-emption on the ground that they lost their co-shareship in the ease holding, as far back as in 1963-64 and 1965-66 respectively; that the splitting up of the jama, was acted upon; and that the pre-emptors did not file any dhakialla since 1963-64 and 1965-66 to show that they were paying rent in the old rate for the seven undivided holdings. The learned Single Judge also relied on Md. Jabed Ali and others v. Rakhal Chandra Mondal and others. 33 DLR (AD) 309 wherein this court held that when a valid order under section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is on record, and the order has been given effect to, the Civil Court is not competent to ignore the order on the ground of finding some irregularity in the tame as a Court of appeal, while dealing with the application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption. That view was reiterated in Khairullah Bhuiyan v. Haji Nurul Alam Chowdhury, 35 DLR( (AD) 333.
